title: Representability in arithmetic: expressing computations

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Arithmetic formulas can describe every total computable function, with each particular answer provable from Robinson's seven axioms.
abstract: An algorithm can add two numbers, decode a finite list, or check a proposed proof. Can the seven axioms of Robinson arithmetic establish the answer to each particular calculation? We show that every total computable function has an arithmetic formula for which they can do exactly this, including ruling out every other answer. The construction records a finite computation by remainders of division, so we first supply the elementary arithmetic that makes those records possible. Along the way, bounded formulas explain why finite numerical checks can be proved without an induction axiom. The conclusion concerns a separate proof for each numerical input; it does not say that Robinson arithmetic proves that the algorithm always terminates.
